# Lab 6.8: Materialized Views for Acceleration

## What We Are Going to Do
Build a dashboard-style materialized view with incremental refresh and `max_staleness`, and see queries rewritten to use it.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create the materialized view.** First make sure the required partition filter from Lab 6.3 is off.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">ALTER TABLE lab06.trips_daily SET OPTIONS (require_partition_filter = FALSE);

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW lab06.mv_daily_company
OPTIONS (enable_refresh = TRUE, refresh_interval_minutes = 30, max_staleness = INTERVAL '4' HOUR)
AS
SELECT DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS day, company, COUNT(*) AS trips, SUM(fare) AS revenue
FROM lab06.trips_daily
GROUP BY day, company;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Query the base table the way a dashboard would.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT company, SUM(fare) AS revenue
FROM lab06.trips_daily
WHERE DATE(trip_start_timestamp) BETWEEN '2023-03-01' AND '2023-03-31'
GROUP BY company ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   **Execution details** shows the plan reading `mv_daily_company`. Bytes processed drops sharply.

3. **[SQL] Add new data and check incremental refresh.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">INSERT INTO lab06.trips_daily (unique_key, company, trip_start_timestamp, fare)
VALUES ('test-1', 'Lab Cab', TIMESTAMP '2023-03-15 10:00:00', 25.0);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Within `max_staleness`, BigQuery can answer from the view without merging the new row. Without `max_staleness`, it combines the view with the new delta automatically.

'SELECT table_name, last_refresh_time, refresh_watermark FROM lab06.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.MATERIALIZED_VIEWS'</span>

5. **[Console] Smart tuning.** Open the **Recommendations** page later (Module 24). BigQuery suggests materialized views based on your repeated queries.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Rewrite | Base-table query served by the view |
| Incremental refresh | Only new data reprocessed |
| `max_staleness` | Faster, cheaper, slightly stale results |
| Monitoring | MATERIALIZED_VIEWS view |
